title: Static typing checks do not respect covariance of overridden method when called from object cast as parent type
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in v4.4.beta3 [06acfccf8], v4.3.stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta3 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10500 CPU @ 3.10GHz (12 threads)

### Issue description

Sorry for the convoluted title, I think this issue is a bit subtle and was unsure if it was a quirk or a bug.

As described in https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/static_typing.html#covariance-and-contravariance, a method that overrides from the base class should be allowed to specify a return type that is a subtype of the base method's return type. However, if a derived class is referred to as its parent type, the error settings ```unsafe_property_access``` and ```unsafe_call_argument``` (both of which must be set to ```error``` to enforce static typing in GDScript) seem to assume the parent method's return type.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set ```debug/gdscript/warnings/unsafe_property_access``` to ```error``` in Project Settings
2. In GDScript, define a class with a method returning a ```Node```, for example
```gdscript
class A:
	func make_node() -> Node:
		return Node.new()
```
3. Define a class that extends the first, overriding the method to return the narrower type ```Node3D```
```gdscript
class B extends A:
	func make_node() -> Node3D:
		return Node3D.new()
```
4. Assign an instance of the subclass to a variable of the type of the superclass
```gdscript
var instance: A = B.new()
```
5. Use the method to make a node and try to access a property only available on the narrower type
```gdscript
print(instance.make_node().position)
```
6. Get error: ```Parse Error: The property "position" is not present on the inferred type "Node" (but may be present on a subtype). (Warning treated as error.)```

With ```debug/gdscript/warnings/unsafe_property_access``` set to ```ignore```, the code works fine and accesses the property without issue.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp_overrides.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18812388/mrp_overrides.zip)
